b50.why: 'Poisson paid for the tower': Lustig stands hands behind his back, not even reaching, as the cash drops between them; slow drift on the hand-over

b51.why: 'took the cash': suitcase pose (lustig_2) walks off past the money on the side table; pan follows him out of the room
'took the train': flipped suitcase walk toward the platform, steam dust; pan_l reverses screen direction so the leaving reads as motion
'left the country, to Vienna': new city plate + chip, Lustig walks in from the left with the case; pull reveals the foreign street

b52.why: 'bought newspapers every morning, and waited': Lustig reading the morning paper at the cafe (lustig_reading_newspaper), a fresh paper slides up; locked frame, time dragging
'Nothing.': cut to the other side, the shrug (lustig_4) as the paper drops empty; pull leaves him small

b53.why: 'No headline': back in rainy Paris, the reader holds a paper that is literally blank (parisian_2 has no text); push into the empty page

b54.why: 'something he could not undo': Poisson alone in the hotel room, hands to cheeks (parisian_1) as the contract falls; push + shake on the realisation
'paid a bribe, to buy a national monument': small Poisson with his cash (clerk_2 fanning notes) as the pull reveals the whole tower he paid for, scale shows the absurdity

b55.why: 'If he went to the police': Poisson walks up sweating and stops short of the whistle-blowing gendarme (police_officer_whistle) at the station door
'the man who tried to bribe a minister, and lost': hard push on the gasp (parisian_1) with handcuffs popping in, he would be the one arrested

b56.why: 'Shame did the work that Lustig no longer had to do': back in Vienna, hands behind his back doing nothing (lustig_3); locked camera, he does not have to move

x17.why: 'Poisson waited for the deal to move': chin-in-hand pondering (clerk_1) by the unopened telegram; pan_r drifts toward the tower in the window
'believing he was part of a secret': Poisson's private smile, flipped to face the room; slow drift around a man keeping a secret that is not real

x18.why: 'Every time he looked at the tower': Poisson struts onto the esplanade chest-out (scrap_dealer_proud), pan_r carries the eye to the tower on the right
'something he thought was his': hand-rubbing greed as the owner's keys pop; pull widens to put the whole tower behind the keys he thinks are his

x19.caption: Weeks passed.
x19.why: 'The tower did not move. Weeks passed.': locked-off hold, the only static camera in the act; small figure waits under an unchanging tower
'slowly, a different feeling started to grow': suspicious raised brow (clerk_1) outside the hotel; slow push as the doubt grows

b57.why: 'Lustig came back to Paris': suitcase arrival walk from the left toward the same Crillon entrance as Act 3; pan_r and chip mark the return
'and did it again': at the Crillon door he turns back to camera with an easy shrug (lustig_4), as if nothing happened last time; pull shows the same entrance

b58.why: 'Another set of dealers, the same hotel': same Crillon salon as Act 3, Lustig presenting (lustig_1) to a new dealer reading the summons letter; pull shows the re-run
'the same script': index finger up mid-pitch (lustig_5), the line he has said before; drift as the rehearsed words roll out, no new props needed

b59.why: 'one of them went to the police': the dealer marches in, the gendarme blows his whistle, flash + handcuffs drop; the scene b55 said never happens now does

b60.why: 'left France that night': hunched sneaking pose (lustig_6) slips out of frame right past the hotel door; pan chases him
'did not even stay to count his luck': rushing to the train, a stray note falls behind him uncounted; pull widens to the platform

x20.why: 'Here is the part most retellings skip. He had already won.': suitcase in hand (lustig_2), flipped, strolling unhurried out of the empty plaza; pan_l = the exit he could have kept
'He had a fortune, and a clean exit': proud grin over the loot (lustig_counting_cash; fallback lustig_5) with banknotes popping by the case, flipped to the right side; push on the fortune

lines: is a thief with a hobby.

x21.why: 'needed the story to keep going': hands behind his back, already plotting (lustig_3), he strolls back toward the lit hotel door; pan_r follows the walk

x22.why: 'what finally caught up with him. Not the police.': the shifty 'about to be caught' hunch (lustig_6), flipped, glancing back; pull shows the empty plaza, no one chasing
'The need to be believed again': he walks back in, finger already up for the next pitch (lustig_5) as a ship sails in to tease America; push on the compulsion

needed_plates.desc: Paris Gare de l'Est interior at night, hand-drawn ink and watercolour matching existing plates: iron-and-glass arched roof, steam locomotive with carriages along the right third (x 65-100%), warm gas lamps, platform clock top-centre, open stone platform floor from y ~65% to bottom across full width, centre-left clear for actors.

Vienna Ringstrasse street at dusk, 1925, same ink-and-watercolour style: Baroque facades and a church spire (Stephansdom-like) right-centre, tram wires, orange-pink sky, gas lamps at x ~12% and ~88%, open cobbled foreground from y ~63% down, centre clear for one or two actors. No Eiffel Tower.

Viennese coffee-house interior in morning light, 1925: marble tables, bentwood chairs, newspaper rack on wooden holders at left (x 0-15%), tall windows onto a Vienna street at right, warm cream walls, open wooden floor from y ~66% down, centre clear for a standing actor.

Exterior of a 1920s Paris commissariat at grey daytime: stone facade with blue-white-red flag and 'POLICE' lamp over a dark double door at right (x 75-92%), wet cobbles from y ~63% down, centre-left open for two actors facing each other.

Hotel de Crillon neoclassical colonnaded facade on Place de la Concorde, daytime warm light, obelisk at left edge, grand arched entrance right-centre with doorman post, wide open cobbled/paved foreground y 64-100%

Palatial hotel salon interior: gilded panelled walls, two crystal chandeliers, tall mirrors, red velvet chairs pushed to the edges, polished parquet floor open y 66-100% full width, centre clear for 2-3 standing figures

needed_poses.desc: Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black beret) walking in right-facing profile mid-stride, brown brass-cornered suitcase in the trailing hand, hurried focused look.

Victor Lustig (navy double-breasted coat, cream scarf, orange pocket square, black beret), front-on, holding an open newspaper low enough to show his face, eyes narrowed with a slow sly smile, one eyebrow raised.
Lustig standing three-quarter right fanning a thick wad of banknotes in both gloved hands, satisfied smirk.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), Andre Poisson, scrap-metal dealer (stout stick figure, brown bowler hat, grey three-piece suit, gold watch chain, moustache), extending a fat envelope of banknotes forward to the right, eager hopeful smile.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), standing front-on with both hands gripping his head, eyes wide, mouth open in dawning horror.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), facing right, one foot forward then frozen, hat clutched to chest, sweat drop, worried brows: about to enter but stopping.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), front-on, shoulders slumped, face red, eyes down, hat in limp hand: publicly shamed.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), standing three-quarter right, hands clasped behind back, gazing patiently out of frame right as if at a window.

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), front-on, finger to lips with a proud insider grin, eyebrows up: thinks he is in on a state secret.
Same scrap dealer in his best suit, walking in profile facing right, chest out, chin up, proud and self-important
Scrap-metal dealer stick figure, stocky, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache, rubbing hands together with hungry wide eyes and grin, facing front

Andre Poisson, i.e. the same scrap-metal dealer as Act 3 (stocky stick figure, grey work waistcoat over rolled sleeves, bowler hat, moustache), front-on, hand on chin, one eyebrow raised, frown: doubt creeping in.
1920s Paris gendarme stick figure, dark blue cape and kepi cap, blowing a whistle, one arm raised pointing right, stern face, facing right
Scrap dealer (flat cap, brown work coat, rolled-up forged contract in hand) facing right, arm extended jabbing the papers forward, angry determined face: reporting a fraud.
Same scrap dealer holding open a cream letter with a red wax seal in both hands, flattered smile, eyebrows up, facing front
